scenes.heading: Sketching simple parabolas
scenes.sub: Read the turning point straight from the equation
scenes.say: What if you could draw a parabola in under a minute, with no table of values? If you know how y equals x squared has been moved, you can.
scenes.caption: What if you could draw a parabola in under a minute, with no table of values? If you know how y = x² has been moved, you can.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Slide a U-shaped sticker up, down, left or right
scenes.science: Changes to y = x² move, stretch or flip the parabola
scenes.breaks: In y = (x − 3)² the graph moves RIGHT 3: the sideways move is opposite to the sign.
scenes.say: Imagine y equals x squared is a U-shaped sticker. You can slide it up, down, left or right, swap it for a skinnier or wider one, or flip it over. Each change to the equation is one move. One catch: x minus three in a bracket moves the graph right, not left.
scenes.caption: Imagine y = x² is a U-shaped sticker. You can slide it, swap it for a skinnier or wider one, or flip it. One catch: (x − 3)² moves the graph right, not left.

scenes.heading: Narrower, wider, flipped
scenes.say: First y equals x squared. Then three x squared, which rises three times as fast, so it is narrower. A half x squared is wider. And negative x squared is flipped upside down. All four still turn at the origin.
scenes.caption: y = x². y = 3x² rises three times as fast, so it is narrower. y = ½x² is wider. y = −x² is flipped. All four turn at the origin.

scenes.heading: Sliding the graph
scenes.say: Now the slides. Adding two outside moves the graph up two. Putting x minus three inside a bracket moves it three to the right, because the bracket is zero when x is three.
scenes.caption: Adding 2 outside moves the graph up 2. (x − 3)² moves it 3 to the right, because the bracket is zero when x = 3.

scenes.heading: Turning point form
scenes.say: Put it all together and you get turning point form: y equals a, times x minus h squared, plus k. The turning point is h, k.

scenes.heading: Sketch y = (x + 2)² − 1
scenes.question: Find the turning point and intercepts of y = (x + 2)² − 1.
scenes.say: The shape is a U, and the turning point is negative two, negative one. When x is zero, y is two squared minus one, which is three. When y is zero, x plus two squared is one, so x plus two is plus or minus one. So x is negative one or negative three.
scenes.caption: Shape ∪, turning point (−2, −1). When x = 0, y = 2² − 1 = 3. When y = 0, (x + 2)² = 1, so x + 2 = ±1. So x = −1 or x = −3.

points: Big a: narrower; small a: wider
Outside number: moves up or down
y = a(x − h)² + k turns at (h, k)
scenes.say: Quick recap. A big a makes a skinny graph, and a negative a flips it. A number outside moves the graph up or down. A number inside the bracket moves it sideways, the opposite way to its sign. Turning point form turns at h, k. Now try the practice questions!
